claim: Human programming errors are usually the end of a chain of cognitive breakdowns (mean 2.3 breakdowns, 1.5 errors per chain), not one slip; 159 breakdowns, 69 roots, 102 errors in 7 novices.
agent_test: Log agent failures as chains (root decision, later errors); count mean chain length and root fraction on 50 failing runs at equal tokens. TrajDebug (a36) already reports 7.62 local errors and 1 critical error per failed trajectory.
caveat: One research group, one system (Alice), 7 novices. a13 reuses the same data.

claim: Breakdowns made while forming hypotheses about a runtime failure (18% of all) caused nearly all rule/skill breakdowns in later code modification (24%): a wrong diagnosis drives a wrong fix.
agent_test: Compare fix success when the diagnosis is checked before editing versus direct edit, same token budget; score the fraction of wrong first hypotheses that lead to an edit.
caveat: Same group (Ko and Myers 2004 formative study, a15: about 50% of errors tied to false hypotheses). Not independent. Ko and Myers text is loose: 'about 18% of all breakdowns' are runtime (skill 8.1 + knowledge 10.1 points, Table 10); the 'nearly all of the 24% modification breakdowns' link is the authors' reading, not a computed attribution.

claim: Programmers consider few hypotheses, usually favor one, and are often wrong at first (about 90% wrong initial guesses, as cited).
agent_test: Force 3 distinct candidate causes before any edit; measure whether the first-listed cause is the true one (expect low) and whether the 3-way set contains it.
caveat: a22 is secondhand (Gilmore, Vessey not opened); the 90% figure is cited by Ko and Myers, not re-measured.

claim: Asking why/why-didn't questions that surface the unchecked assumption speeds human debugging (7.8x in time to diagnosis in scenarios; 10/10 vs 3/10 solved in a 20-person study).
agent_test: Prompt the agent to state the assumption behind each why-did-this-happen question and test it by a probe or trace; equal-token comparison with free-form debugging.
caveat: All by the creators of the Whyline; small samples (6 scenarios, 9 people, 20 people).

claim: Without an external signal, LLM self-review of reasoning does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8 after five calls; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0).
agent_test: Self-review pass vs none at equal tokens on a reasoning set; count correct-to-wrong flips. Prediction: net loss without a tool or test signal.
caveat: a26/c04/c05 are one paper (Huang et al.). Independent support: Tyen (c06) and Olausson (a25). Boundary: tasks with real execution feedback (Chen, Reflexion) differ. Gap search: Kamoi survey (to May 2024) and CRITIC agree. Not yet re-tested on current long-thinking models at equal tokens; d01/d02 suggest reasoning models self-correct injected errors much better.

claim: LLMs are weak at finding the faulty step but can fix it when told where it is; the true location beats a random location.
agent_test: Give the agent a step-level locator (test, trace, or separate verifier) then repair; compare with self-located repair at equal tokens. Tyen: arithmetic +43.92 true location vs +20.39 random.
caveat: Tyen is one paper on CoT traces (GPT-4 52.87% best); Olausson is code. Loss of 11-15 points on already-correct traces when a locator is wrong.

claim: Self-repair of code is limited by the quality of the model's own diagnosis: human feedback lifts repair success from 33.3% to 52.6% (GPT-4, 40 programs, 16 people); at equal sample cost, repair gives 1.05x or less than 1x of pass@k.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare k fresh samples vs 1 sample plus repair with model-written diagnosis vs repair with a stronger or tool-grounded diagnosis.
caveat: One paper (Olausson); GPT-4 and Code Llama on APPS and HumanEval, 2023-era models.

claim: Execution feedback (unit-test results, real traces) is what makes self-debugging work; explanation alone gives only 2-3 points on Spider and nothing on strong models.
agent_test: Ablate access to run results vs explanation-only at equal tokens. Chen: MBPP GPT-4 72.8 to 80.6 with unit tests; Spider GPT-4 73.2 to 73.6 with explanation. LDB (c13): model-written dry-run traces did not help StarCoder, real traces did.
caveat: Chen is one source; LDB supplies an independent second. Small gaps (0.2-1 point) are within the noise of single runs. Gap search: AutoSD shows imagined debugger output reverses the usefulness of the done signal. Gap search: variable-state traces gave the largest ablation drop in TraceCoder (-10.5 points, confounded, d21); raw error text alone lifts all 7 modern models (+4.9 to +30 pp, d22).

claim: Showing real intermediate program state block by block (LDB) beats whole-program self-debugging: HumanEval GPT-3.5 73.8 to 82.9 vs 81.1; up to +9.8%.
agent_test: Give the agent per-block variable values from a real run vs a written dry-run; equal tokens (the trace costs tokens).
caveat: NExT (a31, +26.1 absolute on MBPP-R) involves training, so it does not transfer to a scaffold-only agent. Gains are small and in-benchmark.

claim: LLM debugging difficulty rises with defect type: surface slips are easy, logic and multi-bug cases are hard (GPT-4 93.6% missing colons vs 68.6% operation error, 55.9% quadruple bugs).
agent_test: Sort agent bugs by type; apply extra hypothesis and verification steps only to logic-class bugs.
caveat: DebugBench injects bugs; Wang et al. (c24) find model-made defects are structural; Majgaonkar (a33) shows failure is in reasoning, not navigation. Different datasets, same direction. Gap search: d22 repeats the split with newer models, name errors repaired about 77%, assertion errors about 45%.

claim: Runtime feedback (tracebacks) helps syntax and reference bugs but hurts or fails to help logic bugs.
agent_test: Feed the stack trace vs withhold it, by bug class; check whether the agent anchors on the crash site.
caveat: One benchmark (DebugBench; gpt-4-0613 and gpt-3.5 only). a28 and c11 are the same paper.

claim: Coding agents that fail mostly find the right file but make the wrong fix; failed runs are longer than successes and repeat the same misreading (silent semantic failure).
agent_test: On failing runs measure (a) correct file located, (b) the same hypothesis repeated across retries; test a forced new-hypothesis rule after a failed test at equal tokens.
caveat: Majgaonkar (72-81% located the file), SWE-agent (52.0% of unresolved are incorrect or over-specific implementations), Mehta (68-80% of failing runs silent semantic; 50 tasks). Different harnesses, same pattern. Gap search: SWE-agent 52.0% of 248 failures are wrong or too-narrow implementation; a correct file does not give a correct fix (82.2% and 69.6% repair after a hit). Gap search: for strong models the wrong-patch share is larger than the wrong-file share (d16: 56.9% weighted Edit-Quality vs 19.3% Search on SWE-Agent; 60-69% for GPT-5 and Qwen3-Coder), and flawed reasoning was coded for about 65% of failures (d18).

claim: Agents show action bias: given an already-fixed bug they still edit correct code (60-90% of runs); pre-edit prompt guards did not help.
agent_test: Include solved-already probes; test an explicit is-a-change-needed gate. Prompt-only guards were unhelpful in Mehta, so the gate should use a tool check.
caveat: One paper, n=50 per model; the 60-90% range was not re-verified at figure level. Gap search: a tool gate (linting) raised SWE-agent 15.0 to 18.0, but it guards syntax, not is-a-change-needed. Overthinking paper shows 2025 reasoning models fail the opposite way (too little action). Tool gate for action bias still untested. Gap search: no study of an is-a-change-needed gate was found (gap 6 stays open).

claim: Failed-agent trajectories hold many local errors, most (61.9%) later repaired; one earliest critical error decides failure, and locating it is hard (34.11% macro accuracy vs 25.69% direct prompting).
agent_test: On failing runs, detect the earliest critical step; test rollback to it versus continuing, at equal tokens.
caveat: TrajDebug is one preprint with 50 annotated trajectories; MAST (c25, kappa 0.88; incorrect verification 9.1%, premature termination 6.2%) is a related taxonomy, not a test of this claim. Gap search: Who&When step accuracy best 14.2% (some methods below random), so a log-reading detector is not reliable enough to trigger rollback; SWE-Search shows backtracking with a value signal helps (23% relative). Gap search: DoVer (d20) found several different interventions can each repair the same failed run, so a single 'earliest critical step' may not be well defined.

claim: Passing benchmark tests does not show the defect was fixed: 7.8% of correct-counted SWE-bench patches fail developer tests; 32.67% of passes had solution leakage; resolution fell 12.47 to 3.97% after filtering.
agent_test: Score the agent by hidden stricter tests, not by self-chosen tests, and report both numbers.
caveat: Three independent audits. Absolute rates are specific to old SWE-bench and 2024 models.

claim: Reproduction tests and fixed localize-repair-validate pipelines beat open-ended agent choice at lower cost.
agent_test: Reproduce-first versus none at equal tokens. Agentless +5 points from reproduction-test selection; SWE-agent shows interface (lint guard +3.0) also matters, so effects are confounded.
caveat: Agentless 32.00% on Lite is 2024; stronger agents since; AutoCodeRover SBFL gain small (19 to 22%). Parnin and Orso (a23, unopened) suggest better localization need not help people. Gap search: reproduction tests help as a selector (Agentless +15 fixes, SWT-Bench precision doubled to 47.8% at about 20% recall), but only 94 of 213 reproduction tests verified the true fix. Pipeline vs agent with model and interface fixed is still not tested. Gap search: Coherence Collapse (d16) and the issue-solving failure study (d18) show localisation is not the main failure for strong agents, so a localisation pipeline alone does not explain the K16 gap.

claim: Self-debugging by reflection needs tests: Reflexion Rust ablation shows no gain without test generation or without reflection (0.60 vs 0.68 full).
agent_test: Ablate test generation and reflection separately at equal tokens.
caveat: Ablation on 50 problems only.

claim: There is no independent replication or failed replication of the Ko and Myers (2005) breakdown percentages.
agent_test: None (about the evidence base). Treat the skill/rule/knowledge shares as one 7-person result, not a constant.
caveat: Absence in this search, not proof of absence. A systematic map of 65 bias studies (b05) found zero replications, families of experiments or meta-analyses in software engineering to 2016. Reason 1990, Gilmore, Vessey and Parnin and Orso 2011 were never opened. Treat the 159-breakdown shares as one 7-person result. Gap search: Parnin and Orso 2011 (d24) was opened; it is a localisation-tool study and does not re-measure the shares. Reason, Gilmore, Vessey stay unopened. Still no replication found.

claim: Reasoning models show almost no self-correction blind spot on injected errors, and appending 'Wait' lifts non-reasoning base models close to their reasoning siblings (DeepSeek-V3 0.567 to 0.902 vs R1 0.908).
agent_test: On own diagnosis, compare a forced Wait-style recheck against none at equal tokens, on logic bugs.
caveat: Injected errors, mostly math; one preprint; not code debugging; equal-token cost not measured. Gap search: still tested only on injected errors; no real-code-defect test was found (gap 8 open). Kamoi (d03) and Arimbur (d22) agree that a real signal is what matters.

claim: Real debugger output makes a model's 'done' signal informative (+12.4 points plausible-patch rate); imagined debugger output makes it misleading (-11 points).
agent_test: Same hypothesis loop with real versus model-simulated execution output.
caveat: One paper; small benchmarks; hypothesis loop and debugger confounded.

claim: Generated reproduction tests are a useful selector among candidate patches (Agentless 81 to 96 fixes; SWT-Bench precision to 47.8% at about 20% recall), but a test can reproduce the symptom and not verify the fix (94 of 213).
agent_test: Filter candidate fixes by self-made fail-to-pass test; report precision and recall, and count tests that fail the golden patch.
caveat: Selection gain, not a reproduce-first-versus-open-choice test (see K16).

claim: Current reasoning-model agents on SWE-bench often plan instead of acting; higher overthinking scores go with lower resolve rate, and picking the lowest-overthinking of 2-3 samples gave 27.3-30.3% at lower cost.
agent_test: Cap pure-thinking turns without a tool call; compare with uncapped at equal tokens.
caveat: Early-2025 models; correlational plus a selection intervention.

claim: LLMs are poor at naming the decisive error step in an agent log (best 14.2% step accuracy; all-at-once below random); adding rule-based constraint checks lifts step accuracy by about 13 points but not above 50% on hard sets, so rollback should be triggered by checks, not by an LLM reading the log alone.
agent_test: Compare rollback triggered by test failure or diff size versus by an LLM reading the log, at equal tokens.
caveat: Multi-agent logs, not coding trajectories. Gap search: AgentRx (d19) tau-bench step accuracy judge-only 29.9 vs with violations 42.7; Who&When-style judge 18.8 vs AgentRx 42.7. Not code tasks. DoVer (d20) says the decisive step may not be unique. Edit-commit freeze after a passing test recovered 5 of 5 tested cases (d17); consensus trigger gave +3.0 points, p=0.08.

claim: A tool gate that rejects a syntax-breaking edit and shows the error raised SWE-agent from 15.0% to 18.0% on SWE-bench Lite; after one failed edit the chance of eventually succeeding fell from 90.5% to 57.2%.
agent_test: Add an is-a-change-needed gate (run failing test first) and compare against a prompt-only guard.
caveat: Single model; guards syntax only.

claim: No published study codes LLM agent failures in the Ko and Myers chain form (root breakdown, then error). The nearest are SWE-agent failure categories (52.0% wrong or narrow fix) and MAST (kappa 0.88, 14 modes).
agent_test: Code 100 failed runs with a first-wrong-hypothesis label and a was-it-revisited label.
caveat: Absence in this session's search, which was limited by quota; gap 1 stays open.

claim: Small code patterns (atoms of confusion) raise novice misreading, but only about half replicate in Java: pooled odds ratio 3.82 (95% CI 2.69-5.42); 7 of 14 atoms individually significant.
agent_test: Seed prompts with atoms vs clean twins and count mis-predicted outputs from the agent at equal tokens; check which atoms transfer.
caveat: Original C study (b30) seen only as an abstract (73 programmers). Java replication used 96 novice students on output-prediction snippets. Table text in the PDF is garbled; per-atom odds ratios (b02 range 2.7 to 56) and the b02 note that indentation atoms were not significant are not reliable: the paper text lists 'remove indentation atom' among the 7 significant atoms. Experts untested.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLMs show human-like framing, anchoring and distraction slips: irrelevant framing lines cut Codex accuracy 22.3-30.5 points and were copied in 81% of outputs; a conflicting function name cut accuracy from 100% to 4.4-4.6%; one irrelevant sentence limits math solving; bias cues flip 5.9-35.3% of correct answers.
agent_test: Add a misleading cue (wrong function name, irrelevant line, prior wrong patch) to a debugging task and measure fix rate with and without a rule to restate the spec before editing, at equal tokens.
caveat: Different tasks, models from 2022-2025. Anchoring is the weakest effect in Sovrano (5.9% sensitivity) yet lowers accuracy in Jones's code anchors (read from figures). Jones's GPT-3 anchoring replication had about 41% gibberish outputs.

claim: Telling a model to be aware of bias helps little: models can name the bias and still follow it, and sensitivity grows with reasoning depth (up to 49%).
agent_test: Compare an 'avoid bias' instruction against a structural step (restate spec, list rival causes) at equal tokens.
caveat: Awareness prompts reduced primacy slightly for Llama-2 7B and GPT-4 (b22, read from figures). Rewriting the prompt to remove bias worked better in some models (b21). Results differ by model. Human debiasing evidence is also nil (b06).

claim: Bigger or instruction-tuned models are not freer of bias: instruction tuning and RLHF raise decoy, certainty and belief-bias behaviour over the base model.
agent_test: Run a bias battery on base vs scaffolded model at equal tokens.
caveat: b23 exact percentages not extracted; 2023 models; b20 covers reasoning depth not tuning, so the second source is indirect.

claim: Developers using an LLM assistant show more biased actions (53.7% vs 47.14% overall) and more reversals (29.4%), with fixation (re-pasting the same fix after an error) the worst at 43.4% reversal.
agent_test: Count repeated near-identical patches after a failed test in agent runs; test a rule to change the hypothesis after one failed fix, at equal tokens.
caveat: 14 developers, 2,013 actions, one study. Replication of Chattopadhyay 2020: bias share matched (47.14% vs 45.72%) but reversal rate was 25% vs 52.9%, so the two samples disagree on reversals. Re-checked against the paper this session.

claim: Professional experience did not protect against anchoring when judging code understandability (students and 50 professionals anchored alike; path 0.165, N=256).
agent_test: None direct. Do not assume a stronger model removes anchoring.
caveat: One research group, rating task, not debugging. Effect small.

claim: Cognitive bias research in software engineering is thin: of 65 studies (to 2016) none was a replication, family or meta-analysis, and none gave strong evidence for any debiasing technique; fixation had one study.
agent_test: None (about the evidence base).
caveat: One systematic map; later work (2017-2026) not covered.

claim: One night of sleep loss roughly halves novice code correctness (-49.7%, CI -1.58 to -0.20, N=45) and raises syntax-fixing edits; effects on engagement and process were not established (CIs include zero).
agent_test: None for a stateless agent. Analogy only: degraded state raises skill-level slips.
caveat: Quasi-experiment, novices, one task, test-first development. Re-checked: 23 vs 22 participants, -49.73%.

claim: Code that is surprising to an LLM (perplexity) tracks where humans show a confusion signal: rho 0.47 for confusing snippets vs 0.05 for clean ones; a perplexity detector found 64% of labelled atoms.
agent_test: Use token-level surprise on the agent's own plan or patch as a cheap flag, and compare with no flag at equal tokens.
caveat: 24 people, 72 Java snippets, one model (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B). Correlation, not a test of fix quality.

claim: The most common bug in LLM-written code is misreading the task (misinterpretation 20.77% of 333 bugs); agent failures likewise are mostly silent wrong fixes, not crashes.
agent_test: Add a restate-and-check-the-spec step before editing and count misinterpretation bugs at equal tokens.
caveat: Tambon used 2021-era code models; Mehta and Majgaonkar use agents on SWE-bench-type tasks. Classes differ, direction agrees.

claim: For strong coding agents, most failed SWE-bench runs reach and edit the right functions and still submit a wrong patch (60-69% for GPT-5 and Qwen3-Coder on SWE-Agent and OpenHands; weighted 56.9% vs 19.3% search failures on SWE-Agent).
agent_test: Measure how often an agent edits the right place and still fails; spend verification effort after the edit, not only before it.
caveat: One preprint, reference-patch-based buckets, residual category; weak models fail upstream instead (Qwen3-8B 41.1% Search).

claim: Some agents write a correct patch mid-run and destroy it later (39.7% of Edit-Quality failures on SWE-bench; 5 of 5 tested mid-run edits passed the full tests when re-run). A cheap non-LLM trigger helps a little: consensus-driven confirmation +3.0 points, p=0.08.
agent_test: Add a rule: once a patch passes the failing test, freeze it and require a stated reason plus a passing test to change it; count how often it prevents a lost fix.
caveat: Existence proof on 5 cases; consensus result not significant; precision of the trigger 52.4%.

claim: Agent failures coded by hand show persistence with a failed strategy: about 65% of 150 failed SWE-Bench-Verified instances were traced to flawed reasoning; those runs took 3.5 times more steps; a supervising Expert agent resolved 22.2% (24 of 108) of issues OpenHands had failed.
agent_test: Test the one-failed-fix rule against an external plan review at equal tokens, scored on previously failed issues and on fresh ones.
caveat: One backbone, Python, cause shares approximate, selection on previous failures, no token control.

claim: A trigger that checks steps against constraints (schemas, policies) and passes violations to an LLM judge locates the first unrecoverable step far better than a judge reading the log (tau-bench 18.8 to 42.7; RelWork 32.6 to 61.5; ablation 29.9 to 42.7), yet stays under 50% on tau-bench.
agent_test: Build the rollback trigger from test results and diff checks; compare with an LLM reader at equal tokens on code tasks.
caveat: Not code tasks; GPT-5 judge; critical-step definition differs from Who&When.

claim: Failure hypotheses can be tested by intervention rather than by reading the log: DoVer flipped 18-28% of failed multi-agent trials to success and validated or refuted 30-60% of hypotheses (49% recovered on GSMPlus with AG2).
agent_test: Prefer a cheap experiment over a log reading when checking a root-cause hypothesis; compare to pure resampling.
caveat: Multi-agent web tasks, not code; no resampling control seen; abstract-level numbers.

claim: Among repair signals, the failing message or case beats bare pass/fail by about 13 points (provisional, abstract only), a 'code must change' instruction adds 0.8-1.9 points, and variable-state traces gave the biggest ablation drop (-10.5) in a trace-driven repair loop. No study compares these with the human-feedback 33.3 to 52.6% result.
schema_part: G3 (what feedback to give the agent)
agent_test: Run a three-arm test: pass/fail, failing message, variable state, at equal tokens, plus a human-hint arm.
caveat: d23 abstract only; d21 ablation confounded by extra LLM calls; d22 compares only raw error text. Counted as single-source because no clean controlled comparison exists.

claim: Seeing the symptom or even the faulty line is not understanding the defect: of 10 programmers who clicked the fault line, 9 kept inspecting for about 10 more minutes; some stopped the failure without fixing the fault (Parnin and Orso 2011, 34 students).
agent_test: Require a statement of why the fault caused the failure before accepting a patch; test whether it reduces symptom-only patches.
caveat: Small student sample, a localisation tool, 2011; not a test of the Ko and Myers shares.
